notes.meaning: Moses and the Israelites sing a song of praise to the Lord right after crossing the Red Sea safely. They give all the glory to God alone because He threw the Egyptian army and their horses into the water. True worship keeps its eyes on what God has done rather than on human effort.

The singers proclaim that the Lord gives them power, fills them with joy, and has rescued them from death. He is not a stranger to them, but the faithful God of their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. When believers recognize God as their true rescuer, praise naturally overflows from their hearts.

Scripture calls the Lord a warrior to show that He fights for His people and always wins the battle. His name is the Lord, which reminds everyone that He alone has absolute power and keeps every promise. No earthly army can ever stand against the God who created all things.

Pharaoh sent his finest officers and chariots to destroy Israel, but God hurled them into the Red Sea. The heavy waters covered them completely, and the armored soldiers sank straight to the bottom like stones. God easily brings down the proudest rulers when they set themselves against His plans.

The song praises God's right hand, which stands for His supreme power and skill in breaking the enemy to pieces. The Egyptian army opposed God Himself by attacking His people, so His holy anger burned them up like dry grass. Opposing God's people is the same as opposing God, and it brings certain defeat.

God parted the waters as effortlessly as breathing through His nose, sending a strong wind to divide the sea. The surging currents stood upright like solid walls on both sides so Israel could walk through. God has full control over all nature and can make deep waters stand firm at His command.

The Egyptian pursuers were filled with cruel pride, boasting that they would catch the Israelites, kill them, and take all their riches. Their rapid words show how greedy and confident they were in their own strength. People often feel most sure of success right before God brings their downfall.

With a single breath of wind from God, the sea rushed back and swallowed the entire Egyptian army. Their heavy armor dragged them down so quickly that they sank like weights of lead into the raging deep. Human boasting vanishes in an instant when God decides to act.

Moses asks who can compare to the Lord, proving that no idol or earthly ruler comes close to His greatness. God is completely pure and set apart in His holiness, so great that He must be praised with deep reverence. Remembering God's unmatched majesty helps His people worship Him with true awe.

God raised His hand in judgment, and the sea bed and surrounding earth swallowed up the drowned army. When the Creator fights against the wicked, the whole created world turns against them as well. Those who oppose God find that no place on earth can shield them from His hand.

Because of His loyal love, God redeemed His people, buying them back from slavery, and began guiding them safely along the way. His great strength would lead them all the way to His holy dwelling place in the promised land. Believers can be confident that the God who rescues them will also finish leading them home.

Word of this stunning miracle would spread quickly to neighboring nations like Philistia, Edom, Moab, and Canaan. Deep dread would make these fierce warrior nations freeze like stones instead of attacking Israel as they passed by. When God protects His people, He removes their enemies' courage and paves a safe path before them.

The song looks ahead to the day when God would firmly plant Israel in the hilly country of Canaan as His permanent family inheritance. There He would establish His sanctuary, the sacred place where His people could live in His presence. God does not just deliver His people from trouble; He establishes them in safety near Himself.

The song closes with the joyful declaration that the Lord's kingdom has no end. Pharaoh's proud reign crashed down in a moment, but God's rule will continue through all eternity. It gives believers endless peace to know that their King will reign forever.

This sentence summarizes the miracle by reminding readers of the great contrast between Egypt and Israel at the sea. Pharaoh's horses and chariots were swallowed up when the waters crashed back down, while God's people walked safely across on dry ground. God makes a clear distinction between those who trust Him and those who fight against Him.

Miriam, the sister of Aaron and Moses, led the women with tambourines and holy dancing to celebrate this great rescue. She sang the chorus back to the men, praising the Lord for throwing the enemy's horses and riders into the sea. Giving open, joyful thanks to God is a fitting response whenever He works wonders for His people.

Moses led the people away from the sea into the dry wilderness of Shur, where they traveled for three days without finding any water. Going without water in the desert heat was an intense trial that quickly tested their physical endurance and faith. God often leads His people through difficult places to teach them to depend completely on Him.

When the thirsty travelers finally reached water at Marah, it was too bitter and salty to drink, giving the place its name. Instead of praying, the people complained bitterly against Moses and demanded to know what they would drink. Hard times quickly reveal whether people are relying on faith or merely on what they can see.

Moses brought the crisis directly to the Lord in prayer, and God showed him a piece of wood to throw into the water. As soon as the wood entered the pool, God miraculously made the water fresh and sweet for everyone. God used this event as a test to show the people that He alone can turn bitter trials into blessings.

God promised that if the people would listen closely and obey His commands, He would shield them from the terrible sicknesses He brought on Egypt. He revealed Himself by a new name, the Lord who heals, showing that He is the great physician of body and soul. Walking in obedience to God brings true health, peace, and spiritual protection.

The people next arrived at Elim, an oasis blessed with twelve fresh springs and seventy sheltering palm trees. After suffering through thirst and bitter water, they were able to camp and rest peacefully by plenty of sweet water. God does not leave His children in bitter trials forever, but brings seasons of rest and refreshment right on time.
